original_text: –Scientists conducted a controlledexperimentto test the hypothesis that color patterns have evolved as adaptations that protect animals from predation.–The experiment compared an experimental group consisting of noncamouflaged mice models and a control group consisting of camouflaged models that matched the mice native to each area.–The groups differed by only one factor, the coloration of the mouse models.
explanation: This slide describes Case Study 2 of the scientific method, which tested whether mouse color patterns evolved as protective adaptations against predators. In this controlled experiment, scientists compared an experimental group of noncamouflaged mouse models with a control group of camouflaged mouse models (which matched the native mice of the area). The groups differed by only one factor (the experimental variable): the coloration of the mouse models.

questions.q: In the mouse camouflage experiment (Case Study 2), what was the single factor that differed between the experimental group and the control group?
opts: The size of the mouse models
The location where the models were placed
The coloration of the mouse models
The type of predators in the habitat
